main_text.p: Saporum alii calidi sunt, seu caloris dominiū sequuntur, ut acer, amarus, salsus. alii frigidi, ut acidus, austerus, acerbus, alii temperati, ut dulcis, pinguis, insipidus, si modo sapor dicendus. Acris qualis in pipere, & cæpa deprehenditur, linguam cum calore penetrat, inflammat, mordet. Huius generatio est ex sicco terreo, humido permixto, à calore attenuato adeo, ut partes effervescant: partes dico terrestres & aqueas. Ergo acria medicamenta, sunt calida, sicca, tenuium partium: habent autem vim rarefaciendi, attenuandi, discutiendi. Amarus, qualis in colocynthide, linguam detergit, abradit, exasperatque, cuius causa est vehemens calor humorem consumens: estque medicamentum amarum, calidum, siccum, substantiæ terrestris, ad similitudinem fuliginis aut cineris. minus penetrat, & rarefacit, quam acre: incidit tamen, detergit, meatus aperit. Huic vicinus est salsus, genitus ex sicco terreo, copioso humore perfuso,

page.notes: Marginal notes at the right edge are cut off and only partly legible (fragments such as "fulo, à calore", "sante", "potius", "Frigidi", "qualis", "ergo"); they are not transcribed. Words with a printed hyphen at line ends were joined where the hyphen was printed ("ape-rit" appears as "aperit", "per-fuso" as "perfuso"). Possible faint pencil marks at the lower left of the text were not read.
